tools.name: kanna_info
tools.description: Report which Kanna runtime this client is actually connected to. Returns the exact effective HTTP base URL and parsed host/port, client adapter identity, an allow-listed identity snapshot from the authoritative server /v1/status response, the separately advertised LAN endpoint, capability/write-path health, and an explicit serverStatus error when status cannot be fetched. The connected instance cannot be inferred from a default port, app path, display name, or process name.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

tools.name: kanna_list_machines
tools.description: List the current Kanna machine and every sibling machine currently reachable through the signed-in account's relay connection. Use the returned machine id as machine_id on another tool to read or mutate that machine. The local machine is always returned; relayAvailable and error explain whether remote discovery is currently available.

tools.name: kanna_guide
tools.description: Read the Kanna manual for authoring repository config, workflows, agents, or for operating tasks. The content comes from the running adapter's hot-reloadable tool catalog, so it matches the Kanna version exposing this tool.

params.name: topic
params.description: Manual topic to read.

tools.name: kanna_list_repos
tools.description: List repositories known to the running Kanna desktop server, including each repo's id, name, and local path.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

tools.name: kanna_add_repo
tools.description: Register an existing local git repository with Kanna.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: path
params.description: Absolute path to the local git repository to register.

params.name: name
params.description: Display name for the repository. Defaults to the directory name.

tools.name: kanna_reconcile_repo_metadata
tools.description: Detect a repository's authoritative default branch from origin HEAD, compare it with the recorded metadata, and update the existing repo record by default. This preserves the repo id and its tasks. Set apply=false for a doctor-style drift check without changing metadata. The response includes recorded and detected branch values, provenance for each, drift, and whether an update was made.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Existing repository id from kanna_list_repos. Reconciliation updates this record in place and does not re-register the repository.

params.name: apply
params.description: Apply detected metadata to the existing record. Defaults to true; set false to report drift only.

tools.name: kanna_list_recent_tasks
tools.description: List recent Kanna tasks, newest first by update time. Inside a task session this defaults to that task's repository; pass all_repos for the rare cross-repository view. Set all_machines to discover tasks on every currently reachable account machine; that preserves the account-wide aggregation and returns tasks plus explicit machineErrors. Rows carry a prompt bounded to 500 characters, the latest durable agent name in agent, and the session transport in agentType.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it to use the connected machine, unless all_machines is true.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id to list on one machine. Inside a task session this defaults to the caller task's repository unless all_repos or all_machines is true. Cannot be combined with all_machines because repository ids are machine-local.

params.name: all_repos
params.description: List across repositories instead of applying the caller task's repository default. Cannot be combined with repo_id.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum rows per machine, clamped to 200. Defaults to 50.

params.name: all_machines
params.description: Aggregate tasks account-wide from the connected machine and every currently reachable sibling. Cannot be combined with repo_id because repository ids are machine-local. Every task row has machineId and unreachable peers appear in machineErrors.

params.name: include_closed
params.description: Include closed tasks as well as open tasks.

tools.name: kanna_get_task
tools.description: Fetch one Kanna task's detail. If the id is absent locally but exists on a reachable sibling, the error names that machine and tells you to repeat the call with machine_id. Returns: current workflow name (workflowName), stage, workspace branch (branch), pull-request URL (prUrl), worktree path, blockers, latest stage-run result (latestRun), the revision-round budget (revisionRounds, revisionLimit), and its place in the task tree — parentTaskId upward, childTaskIds downward. childTaskIds lists the task's direct children oldest first and includes closed ones, so a fan-out that lost the ids it created (compaction, a resumed session) rediscovers them here rather than re-listing the repo; a finished child is exactly the one an orchestrator must reconcile. Two independent state dimensions are reported. runtimeState is what the agent process is doing, straight from the daemon's terminal-state detection: 'busy' (working, including blocked inside a long tool or MCP call), 'waiting' (parked on an interactive prompt), 'idle' (settled at its composer between turns), 'exited' (its session ended without a replacement), or absent before any session reported one. readState is whether a human has read the latest output: 'read' or 'unread'. activity is the desktop's display value blending the two ('working' | 'idle' | 'unread') and is kept for existing consumers; it cannot answer either question on its own, because a busy agent nobody has read and a finished one both read 'unread'. Supervising a task means reading runtimeState: 'busy' is a live agent, never a parked one, whatever activity says. deliveredInputCount is how many messages have been delivered into this task's agent session from outside it — operator or manager kanna_send_task_input calls; historical counts may include retired completion notifications. Those messages are written to a live PTY, so a later stage running in a forked worktree with a fresh session cannot see them in any transcript it has: a non-zero count means an instruction history exists and kanna_task_inputs has its text. Never state that nothing was instructed, or that no owner input was sent, without reading kanna_task_inputs first. inputBlocked, when present, means the session is refusing every message delivered into it: 'inherited-draft-unknown' is a session the daemon adopted across a restart or handoff whose composer holds text nobody here saw typed, so submitting would append to an unsent line. It reads as a healthy idle task through activity and runtimeState; do not retry deliveries into it, and say plainly that a human has to resolve that terminal. The agent-facing view omits composer placeholders and suggestions unless the daemon's typed-byte ledger attests that a user actually typed the draft; any remaining composer field is therefore a real typed draft, not session output. Directives that were actually delivered are in kanna_task_inputs; what a task means is in its committed spec.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}).

params.name: agent_view
params.description: Sanitize provider-authored composer suggestions from agent-facing task detail. The catalog defaults this true; human UI callers use the ordinary unsanitized API view.

tools.name: kanna_list_task_children
tools.description: List this task's direct children only, including closed children, in chronological order. Each child exposes its workflow identity (workflowName), plus the agent and verdict from its latest recorded stage run; workflowName distinguishes runless specialty-review children from unrelated direct children. Use this durable history to join and reconcile a fan-out after notifications, compaction, or session resume; it is not an arbitrary closed-task listing.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}).

tools.name: kanna_wait_task
tools.description: Block until a Kanna task finishes or closes, polling its detail. A task counts as finished once a termination is recorded: the task closed, its latest stage run reached a terminal status (succeeded or failed), or its agent session ended without a replacement (runtimeState 'exited'). It never resolves on read state, so a task whose agent is busy inside a long call and whose output nobody has read (activity 'unread') keeps the wait running, and a task whose agent stopped resolves whether activity settled to 'idle' or 'unread'. Returns the task detail plus waitOutcome 'resolved'; read the verdict from latestRun. If the wait window elapses first it returns the latest detail with waitOutcome 'timeout' instead of failing — that is a normal result, so call it again in a loop to keep waiting.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}).

params.name: timeout_secs
params.description: Seconds to wait before returning the latest detail with waitOutcome 'timeout' (clamped to at most 240, so the call returns inside the 300s tools/call timeout MCP clients enforce).

params.name: poll_secs
params.description: Seconds between polls (minimum 1).

params.name: until
params.description: 'finished' resolves when a termination is recorded — the task closes, its latest stage run reaches a terminal status, or its agent session exits; 'closed' resolves only when the task closes.

tools.name: kanna_wait_events
tools.description: Watch several Kanna tasks at once: blocks until any of them emits an event, then returns every event since your cursor plus a new cursor. This is the lossless fan-out primitive — kanna_wait_task blocks on one id and cannot supervise several tasks. Set include_current_activity for a level-triggered manager wait: after the fixed 10-second server debounce, a task already idle, waiting, or exited returns immediately as synthetic task.runtime_settled state, while short idle blips emit nothing. Scope it by task_ids, by parent_task_id (your own id, to watch everything you fanned out without naming it), by repo_id, or by the machine-independent repo_remote_url_hash. Event types: 'task.created', 'run.started', 'run.finished' (payload.status succeeded/failed/cancelled, payload.result), 'stage.changed', 'task.workflow_changed', 'task.pr_created', 'task.revision_requested' (payload.exhausted true means the task is parked for its human — stop waiting), 'task.closed', 'task.runtime_settled' (the unconditional daemon-runtime busy-to-non-busy signal after a fixed 10-second debounce), 'task.awaiting_advance' (a manual-stage main session exited without recording completion), 'task.awaiting_input' (the daemon positively identified an interactive prompt and the agent needs an answer, e.g. via kanna_send_task_input), 'task.activity_changed' (provider-neutral and server-debounced on every activity direction for every provider; payload includes previousActivity, activity, runtimeState, and latestRunFinishedWithoutCompletion, whose true value identifies a parked task awaiting advance; no waiting-prompt placeholder or follow-up polling is required), 'task.merge_signaled' (the task's PR reached the repo's merge agent; payload.source is 'agent' or 'engine'), and 'task.merge_handoff_missing' (the workflow finished a stage that promised the merge handoff with no PR to hand off, so the task was NOT closed — treat it as a failed approval), 'task.input_delivered' (a message was delivered into the task's agent session from outside it; payload.source is 'operator', 'manager', or 'unspecified' (historical retained events may carry 'notify'), payload.preview is a bounded prefix with payload.truncated saying whether it was cut, and the full text is readable with kanna_task_inputs), 'task.input_blocked' (the task's agent session started or stopped refusing messages delivered into it; payload.inputBlocked names the reason while it is blocked ('inherited-draft-unknown': the daemon adopted the session across a restart or handoff and its composer holds text nobody saw typed) and is null when it clears. The session is alive and idle the whole time, so nothing else in the feed says anything is wrong — but every delivery into it is refused, including the pre-close merge handoff, so stop sending and get a human to that terminal), 'task.teardown_failed' (detached workspace teardown failed to start or exceeded its deadline; payload.sessionId and payload.error identify the failure), and 'task.transfer_finalizing' (a cross-machine transfer is shutting the task's agent down so its conversation can be shipped; payload.phase is one of 'wrap-up-sent', 'idle', 'quit-sent', 'exited', 'already-exited', 'degraded'). Prompt text changing while a task remains idle or unread does not produce another event; read waitingPromptSnippet from kanna_get_task when reconciling a stopped task. Event payload fields describe the event-time fact: payload.stage is the stage then, and run events keep their own runId/status/result. Delivery-time state is separate under payload.currentTask (title, stage, activity, stageTransition, and latestRun for finished/awaiting events), so retained history cannot masquerade as today's failure. machineId identifies the source in the payload and aggregate row. Call it in a loop, passing back the short cursor handle you were given unchanged: events that fire between two calls are delivered on the next one, each exactly once. Omit the cursor on the first call to receive the retained history. A handle expires after 10 minutes without use or when its issuing process restarts; the returned error tells you to omit it and safely replay retained history. Legacy full cursor formats remain accepted and upgrade on resume. An elapsed window returns waitOutcome 'timeout' with no events — a normal result, not an error. Native fixed task/repo scopes use one sequence watermark. Native parent_task_id cursors bind that same global watermark to the parent id in a constant-size cursor; membership is evaluated at each read checkpoint, so reparenting never rewinds acknowledged events and newly eligible events after the checkpoint are delivered without cursor growth. hasMore true means another batch is already waiting, so call again immediately. Without machine_id, the connected kanna-server aggregates task, parent, and repository scopes across every sibling machine currently reachable through the account relay, tags every event with machineId, and returns machineErrors for stale or unreachable peers without advancing their native cursors; reconnecting peers catch up from retained history. Repository scope is matched by remote URL hash, not installation-local repo id. Per-machine checkpoints inside server ks1 and MCP km1 aggregates are emitted in one canonical ke1 envelope; deployed bare numeric, p3, kc1, and short-handle values remain accepted and normalize on resume. In kanna-mcp, the existing task_ids fan-in still covers tasks on different currently reachable machines and returns a short client-held aggregate cursor; legacy km1 aggregate cursors remain accepted. A machine_id pins the entire wait to one machine. Each MCP call remains clamped to 240 seconds so clients that abort tools/call around 300 seconds do not discard its result. For an arbitrarily long push-equivalent manager wake, run `kanna-cli task watch` as a background process; it loops this same feed, owns cursor hygiene, and exits when actionable work arrives.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_ids
params.description: Task ids (or branch names) to watch, e.g. the child tasks you created. Required unless parent_task_id or repo_id is given.

params.name: parent_task_id
params.description: Watch every task fanned out under this parent instead of naming ids: pass your own task id and you get your children's events without remembering what you created. Re-resolved on every call, so a child created after you started watching is in scope on the next one. Direct children only, and the parent's own events are excluded — the same set kanna_get_task reports as childTaskIds. Ignored when task_ids is given; takes precedence over repo_id.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Watch every task in this local repository and matching copies on sibling machines. Inside a task session an otherwise unscoped wait defaults to the caller task's repository. The server resolves this installation-local id to the repository's remote URL hash. Ignored when task_ids or parent_task_id is given.

params.name: repo_remote_url_hash
params.description: Watch matching repository copies on every machine by the remoteUrlHash returned from kanna_list_repos. Use this when no local repo id is available. Ignored when task_ids, parent_task_id, or repo_id is given.

params.name: local_only
params.description: Keep this request on the selected machine and return its native cursor. Used by compatibility adapters that already aggregate per-machine waits; ordinary callers should omit it.

params.name: include_current_activity
params.description: Make the wait level-triggered for manager activity. In addition to durable events, return an immediate synthetic task.runtime_settled row for every scoped task already idle, waiting, or exited for the fixed 10-second server debounce. Short idle blips emit nothing. This uses daemon runtime state only, never human read/unread activity, so a restarted manager cannot miss parked work. Synthetic rows share the response limit with durable events; pass the opaque cursor back and drain while hasMore is true to page every settled task exactly once for that cursor. Keep this true while shepherding tasks; after servicing or deliberately ignoring a still-idle task, remove that task from an explicit task_ids scope.

params.name: short_cursor
params.description: Return a short process-local cursor handle instead of the legacy encoded checkpoint. Keep this enabled for agent use. The handle expires after 10 minutes without use or when the issuing process restarts; recovery is omitting the cursor and replaying retained history.

params.name: from
params.description: On a cursorless first call, set this to 'now' to establish the durable event checkpoint at the current tail. With include_current_activity true, already-settled scoped tasks are still returned as synthetic current-state rows. Omit it to preserve the retained-history replay contract. Once a cursor exists, the cursor is authoritative.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Short cursor handle returned by the previous call; pass it back unchanged. It independently checkpoints durable sequence progress and include_current_activity settled-row paging on every machine, so durable events arriving between pages are not lost. Omit on the first call to receive retained history and current settled state for the scope. Legacy full cursors remain accepted.

params.name: timeout_secs
params.description: Seconds to block before returning waitOutcome 'timeout' with no events (clamped to at most 240, so the call returns inside the 300s tools/call timeout MCP clients enforce).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum durable plus synthetic rows in one response (1-500, default 100). hasMore true means at least one native or aggregate-machine continuation remains; call again immediately with the returned cursor until hasMore is false.

tools.name: kanna_notify_mobile
tools.description: Send an operator-facing push notification to Kanna Mobile through the relay. Delivery to registered devices reports acceptedCount, failedCount, and token-free provider failure reasons. Use this for meaningful long-running-task milestones or when the operator needs to act. When task_id is present, tapping opens that task.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: title
params.description: Short notification title shown to the operator.

params.name: body
params.description: Concise notification message shown to the operator.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Optional durable Kanna task id to open when the operator taps the notification.

tools.name: kanna_set_task_workflow
tools.description: Change an open task's workflow and pin the new workflow definition. The new workflow must contain a stage with exactly the task's current stage name; incompatible switches are rejected without changing the task. A running stage run and its live session are left untouched: the newly pinned workflow governs the task when that run next transitions. Revision rounds already spent carry over, and changing a workflow does not change the repo's sticky creation-time workflow choice.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}) whose workflow should change.

params.name: workflow_name
params.description: Workflow definition to pin. Retired built-in aliases still resolve (for example, 'default' resolves to 'no-review' unless the repo defines its own 'default' workflow).

tools.name: kanna_task_logs
tools.description: Fetch recent agent-session log lines for a Kanna task, oldest first.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}).

params.name: tail
params.description: Maximum number of most-recent log lines to return. Defaults to 50.

params.name: agent_view
params.description: Remove non-typed composer suggestion rows from agent-facing logs. A daemon-attested typed draft remains clearly labeled as a draft.

tools.name: kanna_task_inputs
tools.description: Read a Kanna task's durable instruction history: every message delivered into its agent session from outside that session, oldest first. Each record carries the full message text, the time it was delivered, the stage and stage run that were live when it landed, and a caller-declared source — "operator" (a human, or their words relayed), "manager" (an orchestrating agent on its own authority), "unspecified" (the client declared nothing), or historical "notify" rows from the retired completion-injection path. These messages are written to a live PTY and appear in no transcript a later stage inherits, so this is the only durable place they exist: a review stage or dispatcher runs in a forked worktree with a fresh session and must read this before making any claim about what was or was not instructed. total is the full count and inputs is the most recent tail window, so a truncated window is visible rather than silent. Stage prompts, post prompts, and revision feedback are not here — they are already durable on the task's stage runs.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Task id (stable across stages) or one of the task's branch names (task-{id} or task-{id}-{n}).

params.name: tail
params.description: Maximum number of most-recent records to return, clamped to 500. Defaults to 100.

Inside a task session this defaults to that task's repository; pass all_repos for the rare cross-repository search. Set all_machines for the existing account-wide result. Result rows carry only a prompt bounded to 500 characters, the latest durable agent name in agent, and the session transport in agentType.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: query
params.description: Text matched (case-insensitive) against task display names and prompts.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id to search on one machine. Inside a task session this defaults to the caller task's repository unless all_repos or all_machines is true. Cannot be combined with all_machines because repository ids are machine-local.

params.name: all_repos
params.description: Search across repositories instead of applying the caller task's repository default. Cannot be combined with repo_id.

params.name: all_machines
params.description: Aggregate tasks account-wide from the connected machine and every currently reachable sibling. Cannot be combined with repo_id because repository ids are machine-local. Every task row has machineId and unreachable peers appear in machineErrors.

params.name: include_closed
params.description: Include closed tasks as well as open tasks.

tools.name: kanna_list_repo_tasks
tools.description: List Kanna tasks for a repository.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id from kanna_list_repos.

tools.name: kanna_list_agents
tools.description: List every resolved named agent definition available to task creation for a repository. Each result includes the invokable name, resolved frontmatter description, definition default provider, model, and effort, and source (built_in, repo_override, or repo_authored). A null defaultProvider means task creation falls back to the configured user default. Repo AGENT.md files win over built-ins by name, and repo EXTEND.md files are already layered into the reported defaults. Definitions declaring `visibility: internal` (stage posts Kanna binds itself, such as commit and approve) are excluded from this listing but still resolve when named explicitly.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id from kanna_list_repos.

tools.name: kanna_create_task
tools.description: Create a new Kanna task: forks a worktree and starts the workflow's first stage agent with the prompt. When called from a Kanna task session, repo_id defaults to the current task's repo. `agent` optionally names any resolved agent definition returned by kanna_list_agents to run the task's first stage with, overriding the workflow stage's own agent binding. Ordinary durable repository work is top-level by default, even when an orchestrator creates it. Set parent_task_id only for a genuine semantic subtask in a decomposition or fan-out. Observe completion through kanna_wait_events for fan-out or kanna_wait_task for a single task.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id from kanna_list_repos. Optional inside a Kanna task session, where it defaults to the current task's repo.

params.name: prompt
params.description: Task prompt given to the first stage's agent.

params.name: display_name
params.description: Short human-readable task title shown in the sidebar. Omitting it does not derive a title: the task falls back to the prompt text itself, clipped to fit, so tasks whose prompts share an opening line become indistinguishable. Always pass one when creating several tasks from a template.

params.name: workflow_name
params.description: Workflow to run, by review depth: 'no-review', 'single-reviewer', or 'specialized-reviewers'. Defaults to the repo's configured workflow. Internal workflows Kanna binds itself are not choices here — only name one if an agent definition tells you to.

params.name: agent
params.description: Any resolved agent definition name. kanna_list_agents lists the choices — definitions declaring `visibility: internal` are excluded from that listing but still resolve here when an agent definition tells you to name one. It runs the first stage instead of the stage's own agent binding; repo overrides and EXTEND.md layering are honored.

params.name: base_ref
params.description: Git ref to fork the task's branch and worktree from. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

params.name: agent_provider
params.description: Explicit agent provider id: 'claude', 'copilot', 'codex', 'opencode', or 'antigravity'. When omitted, Kanna uses the selected stage or agent definition's provider candidates, then the configured user default.

params.name: agent_type
params.description: 'pty' runs the agent CLI in an interactive terminal session; 'agent' runs it headless via the SDK.

params.name: model
params.description: Model id passed verbatim to the selected agent CLI: Claude uses '--model <id>', Copilot uses '--model=<id>', and Codex/OpenCode use '-m <id>'; Antigravity rejects model overrides. An explicit value overrides agent-definition frontmatter; omit it to use the provider default. Kanna does not maintain a model-id allowlist.

params.name: effort
params.description: Provider-native reasoning effort passed without normalization. Codex uses model_reasoning_effort and validates against the selected model; Claude uses --effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); Copilot uses --effort (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max); OpenCode uses --variant and validates against the selected model; Antigravity uses --effort (low|medium|high). Explicit task effort overrides repo agentProviders effort, then layered agent-definition frontmatter.

params.name: permission_mode
params.description: Permission mode passed to the agent CLI, in camelCase: 'dontAsk', 'acceptEdits', or 'default'.

params.name: parent_task_id
params.description: Existing durable work-item id to nest this task under as a genuine semantic subtask in a decomposition or fan-out. Omit for ordinary top-level work and when the creator merely owns, assigns, or monitors it.

params.name: allowed_tools
params.description: Allow-listed tool names passed to the agent CLI.

params.name: blocker_task_ids
params.description: Task ids that must finish before this task; it shows as blocked until they do.

tools.name: kanna_signal_agent
tools.description: Find or create a singleton task for an agent in a repo and send it an ordinary policy request. The response's 'created' says which happened: the provider and effort overrides below only apply to a task this call creates, because an already-running singleton keeps the session it was spawned with. Requests may be sent to the merge singleton for its repo-defined policy to assess. A singleton whose session the daemon inherited may refuse delivered input; that fails with input_blocked and marks the singleton's own task inputBlocked, which is a human's to resolve, not a retry. A singleton whose terminal holds an unsent human line fails with input_held_by_draft: the request is queued at the daemon rather than delivered, so do not resend it — it goes out when that terminal submits.

params.name: machine_id
params.description: Machine id from kanna_list_machines. Omit it, or pass the current machine id, to use the local machine connected to this client.

params.name: repo_id
params.description: Repository id from kanna_list_repos.

params.name: agent
params.description: Agent definition name to signal (e.g. 'merge-master').

params.name: message
params.description: Message delivered to the agent's terminal session as input.

params.name: agent_provider
params.description: Explicit agent provider id for a singleton task this call creates: 'claude', 'copilot', 'codex', 'opencode', or 'antigravity'. It overrides the agent definition's own provider candidates and the configured user default, so pass it to run e.g. the merge agent as claude when the default would pick another provider. Ignored when the agent's task is already running.

params.name: effort

tools.name: kanna_signal_merge_handoff
tools.description: Send the resolved task, PR, head, base, and summary to the repo's merge singleton as an ordinary policy request. The merge agent applies the repository's checked-in policy; Kanna does not attest approval eligibility or bind the request to saved branch metadata. If the merge singleton's session refuses delivered input the call fails with input_blocked and the singleton's task reports inputBlocked; the handoff was not made, so leave the task open and say a human must clear that terminal. If that terminal holds an unsent human line the call fails with input_held_by_draft: the handoff is queued at the daemon, not delivered, so leave the task open and do not resend — it goes out when that terminal submits.

tools.name: kanna_send_task_input
tools.description: Send ordinary input text to a Kanna task's live daemon PTY session as one logical message with its own Enter. Delivery is live-session-only and fenced to the PTY process ID observed before acceptance while holding the task's lifecycle lease. If raw desktop or mobile terminal input has opened an unsent draft, the daemon queues the logical message FIFO until that draft crosses its next producer-declared submission boundary and the call fails with reason input_held_by_draft; the queue survives client/server reconnects and daemon handoff, but is never carried into a later run or stage. If no live input-capable agent session exists, or that session is replaced before acceptance, the call fails with reason no_live_agent_session and reports the latest run status and finish time when available; use kanna_resume_task to preserve provider context when possible, or kanna_rerun_stage to start fresh. An input_held_by_draft failure means a human has an unsent line at that terminal: the message was accepted into the daemon's queue but was NOT delivered, is not recorded in kanna_task_inputs, and will be written when that terminal submits — do not send it again, or a second copy will be queued. A delivery_uncertain failure means the daemon may already have accepted the message and it must not be retried blindly. An input_blocked failure means the daemon refused to submit at all because it inherited that session and its composer holds text it never saw typed; nothing was delivered, retrying changes nothing, and the target task now reports inputBlocked — report it and leave it to a human at that terminal. This can steer a merge singleton under its repo-defined policy. Every accepted delivery is recorded durably against the task and is readable afterwards through kanna_task_inputs, so a later stage can see what was instructed here; an uncertain delivery is deliberately not recorded. Set source to say who is speaking.

guides.title: Kanna Repository Configuration
guides.summary: Repository configuration lives under `.kanna/`. Put committed, portable behavior in `.kanna/config.json`; put one-machine operational overrides in the gitignored `.kanna/config.local.json`. New config files should declare `"$schema": "https://schemas.kanna.build/config.schema.json"`.

sections.title: Schema declaration
sections.body: Set `$schema` to `https://schemas.kanna.build/config.schema.json` in every new `.kanna/config.json` and `.kanna/config.local.json`. Kanna publishes the schema with each merged version so editors and agents can discover supported fields and their semantics.

sections.title: Committed and local layers
sections.body: `.kanna/config.json` is the shared repository contract. `.kanna/config.local.json` is read from the open checkout's working tree, never from the origin snapshot, and is deep-merged over the committed file with local values winning. Local config may contain only `agentProviders`, `workflow`, `ports`, `setup`, `teardown`, and `test`; an unknown key, invalid JSON, or invalid value fails definition resolution and names the file. `agentProviders` and `ports` merge entry by entry, with a local entry replacing the committed entry of the same name. Every other permitted key replaces wholesale, and arrays never concatenate. Keep local config gitignored and do not put task-defining fields such as `vars`, `flavors`, `workspace`, `stage_order`, or reserved ports in it.

sections.title: Lifecycle commands
sections.body: `setup`, `teardown`, and `test` are arrays of shell commands run from the repository or task worktree. `setup` prepares each new workspace before its agent starts. `teardown` runs best-effort when a task leaves a workspace. `test` records the repository's canonical verification commands for agents and workflows. Because local arrays replace rather than append, repeat every command that should remain when overriding one of these keys locally.

sections.title: Ports and workspace values
sections.body: `ports` maps environment-variable names to base ports; Kanna reserves task-specific ports and exports the resolved values so parallel worktrees do not collide. `vars` provides committed string substitutions for agent prompts. `workspace`, `stage_order`, `reserved_ports`, and `reserved_port_offsets` are committed task semantics and cannot appear in local config.

sections.title: Workflow and flavors
sections.body: `workflow` selects the repository's default workflow by name. Kanna resolves a repo-authored `.kanna/workflows/<name>.json` before the bundled workflow of the same name. Workflow and agent definitions are public/listed by default; `visibility: internal` hides an effective definition from listings without preventing explicit resolution, and a repo override must redeclare it to remain internal. `flavors` selects a built-in variant by agent role (for example `"pr": "draft-pr"`); an explicit stage selector such as `pr@draft-pr` wins. Run `kanna-cli guide workflows` or call `kanna_guide {"topic":"workflows"}` before authoring a workflow.

sections.title: Provider, model, and effort resolution
sections.body: `agentProviders` maps exact agent names or `*` globs to a provider name or to `{ provider, model, effort }`; `provider` may be an ordered candidate list. Exact keys beat globs. Among matching globs, the most non-`*` characters wins and lexical order breaks ties. Selection precedence is: explicit task or stage override; matching `agentProviders` entry (including the local layer); layered `AGENT.md`/`EXTEND.md` frontmatter; global default provider. A rerun, resume, revision, or recovery reproduces the recorded run's provider as an explicit override, while a plain stage advance re-resolves the chain and uses the task's stamp only as the final fallback. Provider-specific model and effort values are layer-coherent: Kanna never combines them across providers or layers. It walks the same chain and takes the first value from a layer that would itself select the resolved provider. In an ordered provider list, model and effort belong only to the leading candidate; fallback candidates use a lower coherent layer or their own stamped/default values.

guides.title: Kanna Workflow Authoring
guides.summary: A workflow is an ordered set of stages stored at `.kanna/workflows/<name>.json`. Repo definitions override bundled definitions by name. Prefer selecting a maintained built-in in `.kanna/config.json` unless the repository needs different stages or policies.

sections.title: Definition shape
sections.body: A workflow requires `name` and a non-empty `stages` array and should declare `"$schema": "./schema.json"`. It may define `description`, named `environments` with setup/teardown commands, and `revision_limit` (default 5 agent-requested rounds; `0` means unlimited). Each stage requires `name` and `policy.transition` (`manual` or `auto`), and may set `agent`, `prompt`, `agent_provider`, `environment`, and a `post`. Stage prompts support Kanna runtime variables such as `$TASK_PROMPT`, `$BRANCH`, `$BASE_REF`, `$PREV_RESULT`, and `$PREV_MAIN_RESULT`.

sections.title: Stages, transitions, and posts
sections.body: A manual transition waits for explicit advancement; an auto transition advances after the agent records successful completion. `policy.revision_transition` controls completion after entering that stage through a revision and defaults to `transition`. Advancing to an ordinary next stage forks a fresh branch, worktree, and agent session from the committed prior tip, so only committed work crosses the boundary. A stage `post` is different: it is tail work injected into the stage's running session before transition; its `agent` is the fallback if that session is dead.

sections.title: Visibility
sections.body: Top-level `visibility` is `public` by default. `internal` removes the workflow from listings and pickers but never prevents explicit resolution by name. Visibility belongs to the effective definition: a repo file shadowing an internal built-in must declare `internal` again to remain unlisted; omitting it deliberately promotes the workflow to a public choice.

sections.title: Built-in choices
sections.body: The public built-ins are `no-review`, `single-reviewer`, and `specialized-reviewers`, ordered by review depth. They all begin with implementation plus a commit post and end with PR creation plus an approve post. `specialty-review` and `architect-consultation` are internal workflows explicitly bound by orchestration; do not offer them as ordinary user choices.

guides.title: Kanna Agent Authoring
guides.summary: Agent roles live at `.kanna/agents/<name>/AGENT.md`. A repo `AGENT.md` replaces the bundled definition of the same name; `EXTEND.md` layers repository-specific changes onto the resolved definition without copying it.

sections.title: AGENT.md frontmatter and prompt
sections.body: An agent file is Markdown with optional YAML frontmatter followed by the prompt body. Common frontmatter keys are `name`, `description`, `agent_provider` (one provider or an ordered list), `model`, `effort`, `permission_mode`, `allowed_tools`, and `visibility`. Provider names and model/effort vocabularies are provider-specific. `permission_mode` is `default`, `acceptEdits`, or `dontAsk` (camelCase). The body is the instruction prompt and may use config and runtime variables.

sections.title: Overrides, extensions, and flavors
sections.body: A repo `.kanna/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` fully overrides the bundled agent of that name. Prefer `.kanna/agents/<name>/EXTEND.md` when the bundled behavior should remain and only repository-specific prompt text or frontmatter needs layering; Kanna reads extensions only from the open repo, never bundled resources. Built-in variants live under `flavors/<flavor>/AGENT.md` and can be selected through config `flavors` or an explicit `role@flavor` selector. An extension is role/flavor-scoped and layers after the resolved base definition.

sections.title: Provider coherence and precedence
sections.body: Provider selection is resolved before provider-specific model and effort. The precedence chain is explicit task/stage override, matching repo/local `agentProviders`, layered agent frontmatter, then the global default. Kanna takes model and effort only from a layer that would itself select the resolved provider; it never builds an invalid combination by borrowing values written for another CLI. In an ordered candidate list, values beside the list belong to its first provider only.

sections.title: Visibility
sections.body: Agent frontmatter `visibility` defaults to `public`. `internal` keeps the effective agent out of listings while explicit references still resolve. A repo override decides visibility for the effective definition, and `EXTEND.md` may override it.

guides.title: Kanna Task Operations
guides.summary: A task is a durable work item with a prompt, workflow state, run history, blockers, and a sequence of ephemeral workspaces. Prefer Kanna MCP tools for operations; use the instance-local `kanna-cli` only as a fallback.

sections.title: Identity and workspaces
sections.body: `KANNA_TASK_ID` is stable across stages. A normal stage transition forks a new branch and worktree from the committed tip, so commit everything that must cross the boundary. Do not infer task visibility from stage: `closedAt` determines whether a task is closed, and blockers come from blocker records. Do not push or open a PR unless the current stage explicitly asks.

sections.title: Completion and supervision
sections.body: Record a verdict with `kanna_complete_stage` when the stage prompt requires it; `success` may auto-advance and `failure` stops advancement. Use `kanna_wait_events` to supervise several tasks and `kanna_wait_task` for one. Read `runtimeState`, not blended `activity`, to decide whether an agent is busy, waiting, idle, or exited. `task.awaiting_input` is the positive interactive-question signal. Composer text is not an instruction unless its attestation is `typed`.

sections.title: Inputs and task terms
sections.body: Delivered input is durable and readable through `kanna_task_inputs`; terminal bytes alone are not the record. A non-zero `deliveredInputCount` means instruction history exists. Keep the task's actual terms in `docs/task-specs/<task-id>.md` and update it with owner directives or review decisions so later stages in fresh worktrees share the same contract.
